name: Adbeel
title: Ishmael's third son and tribal prince
summary: Adbe'el was the third of Ishmael's twelve sons and thus a grandson of Abraham through the servant woman Hagar. He is mentioned in the genealogies in Genesis and 1 Chronicles among the twelve Ishmaelite tribal princes who settled in the Arabian region. Together with his brothers, Adbe'el forms a concrete fulfillment of God's promise to Abraham that Ishmael would become the father of twelve princes and grow into a great nation (Gen 17:20). Although the Bible gives no further details about Adbe'el's personal history, scholars have pointed to a possible connection between his descendants and the tribe Idiba'il, known from Assyrian cuneiform texts. His place in the genealogy testifies to God's faithfulness in fulfilling His promises even outside the covenant line through Isaac.

keyEvents.title: The Birth and Lineage of Adbe'el
keyEvents.description: Adbe'el is listed as the third of Ishmael's twelve sons, all of whom became leaders of their respective tribes.

keyEvents.title: Ishmael's Twelve Sons as Tribal Princes
keyEvents.description: Ishmael's sons, including Adbe'el, settled in the region from Havilah to Shur, east of Egypt, and became twelve tribal princes in fulfillment of God's promise to Abraham.

keyEvents.title: God's Promise of Twelve Princes from Ishmael
keyEvents.description: God promised Abraham that Ishmael would become the father of twelve princes and a great nation. Adbe'el was part of the fulfillment of this promise.

keyEvents.title: Adbe'el in the Genealogies of Chronicles
keyEvents.description: Adbe'el is again mentioned in the genealogy in 1 Chronicles, confirming his place among Ishmael's twelve sons.

keyEvents.title: Ishmael's Death and Descendants
keyEvents.description: Ishmael lived 137 years, and his sons, including Adbe'el, established themselves as tribal princes in the Arabian desert.

versions.summary: Adbe'el was the third son of Ishmael, who was Abraham's firstborn son through Hagar. He is mentioned in the genealogies in Genesis and 1 Chronicles as one of Ishmael's twelve sons, who became the ancestors of twelve tribes in the Arabian region. Little is known about his personal life beyond his place in the genealogy.
versions.title: Ishmael's third son
versions.reason: [minor] The role 'patriarch' may be somewhat misleading for Adbe'el, as he is primarily known as a tribal father or tribal prince rather than a patriarch in the traditional biblical sense (patriarchs usually refer to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob). 'Tribal prince' or 'tribal father' would have been more precise.; [major] According to Gen 25:13-15, Ishmael's twelve sons are: Nebajot, Kedar, Adbe'el, Mibsam, Mishma, Dumah, Massa, Hadad, Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedmah. The list of siblings is not missing anyone, but the name 'Hadad' should be verified – in some texts it reads 'Hadad', while others have 'Hadar'. The Hebrew base text in Gen 25:15 likely has 'Hadad' (חדד), which is also confirmed by 1 Chr 1:30.; [critical] First Chronicles has bookId 13, which is correct. But the verse 1 Chr 1:29 should be verified – 1 Chr 1:29 actually mentions the first sons of Ishmael including Adbe'el, so this is correct.; [major] Footnotes are missing. For a biblical figure like Adbe'el, footnotes should be added regarding the etymology of the name, possible archaeological/historical connections, and theological significance.; [minor] The summary is good, but could mention the theological significance of Adbe'el being part of the fulfillment of God's promise to Abraham that Ishmael would become the father of twelve princes (Gen 17:20).

versions.summary: Adbe'el was the third son of Ishmael, who was Abraham's firstborn son through the servant woman Hagar. He is mentioned in the genealogies in Genesis and 1 Chronicles as one of Ishmael's twelve sons, who became tribal princes in the Arabian region. Adbe'el represents part of the fulfillment of God's promise to Abraham that Ishmael would become the father of twelve princes and a great nation (Gen 17:20). Little is known about his personal life beyond his place in the genealogy, but his descendants may possibly be linked to the tribe Idiba'il known from Assyrian sources.

footnotes.text: The name Adbe'el (Hebrew: אַדְבְּאֵל) likely means 'God's discipline' or 'disciplined by God.' The name element 'el' (אֵל) refers to God, while 'adb' may be linked to the Hebrew/Semitic concept of discipline or correction.

Some scholars have attempted to identify Adbe'el's descendants with the Arabian tribe Idiba'il, mentioned in Assyrian cuneiform texts from the time of Tiglath-Pileser III (ca. 745–727 BC). The tribe Idiba'ilu served as guardians of the Egyptian border on behalf of the Assyrian empire.

The twelve sons of Ishmael as tribal chiefs structurally mirror the twelve tribes of Israel that came from Jacob. This parallel underscores God's faithfulness in fulfilling His promises to both Ishmael and Isaac, even though the covenant line went through Isaac.

The area where Ishmael's sons settled—from Havilah to Shur—likely corresponds to the northwestern part of the Arabian Peninsula and the Sinai region, an important trade area along the incense route in ancient times.

In rabbinic tradition, Ishmael's twelve sons receive less attention than Jacob's twelve sons, but they are recognized as fulfilling the promise in Gen 17:20. Some midrash texts comment that Ishmael's sons received their blessing in this world, while Isaac's descendants received the covenant promise for the future.
